quests.question:
Hi Farah, Mr. Dunne asked me to forward you the vendor contract. He wants you to review it before Thursday's call and send comments on the payment terms.
What is 'it' pointing back to?
quests.sentence: Hi Farah, Mr. Dunne asked me to forward you the vendor contract. He wants you to review it before Thursday's call and send comments on the payment terms.
quests.hint: What was forwarded to be reviewed?
quests.explanation: The pronoun 'it' is the object of 'review'. The item forwarded and needing review is the vendor contract; the payment terms are only part of the comments.

quests.question:
Ms. Suarez told the two analysts that the client had rejected the forecast and that they would have to redo it before the board meeting.
Who is 'they' pointing back to?
quests.sentence: Ms. Suarez told the two analysts that the client had rejected the forecast and that they would have to redo it before the board meeting.
quests.hint: Who has to redo the work?
quests.explanation: 'They' is plural, so it cannot be Ms. Suarez or the client. The analysts made the forecast and are the ones who must redo it.

quests.question:
The HR team sent staff a survey about the new rota. Many said it was confusing, so they are drafting a clearer version.
Who is meant by 'they'?
quests.sentence: The HR team sent staff a survey about the new rota. Many said it was confusing, so they are drafting a clearer version.
quests.hint: Who is responding to the complaints?
quests.explanation: Look closely: 'they' is drafting a new version, and the HR team owns the rota. Staff are the ones who complained.

quests.question:
The tutor returned the essays to the students and asked them to read her comments before the next seminar.
Who is meant by 'her'?
quests.sentence: The tutor returned the essays to the students and asked them to read her comments before the next seminar.
quests.hint: Whose comments are on the essays?
quests.explanation: 'Her' is feminine singular, so it cannot be the plural students. The comments are the tutor's, since she marked the work.

quests.question:
Kai emailed his supervisor about the lab schedule, but she hadn't replied by Monday, so he asked the department secretary to check whether it had been updated.
What is meant by 'it'?
quests.sentence: Kai emailed his supervisor about the lab schedule, but she hadn't replied by Monday, so he asked the department secretary to check whether it had been updated.
quests.hint: What could be updated?
quests.explanation: 'It' is singular and non-human. What might have been updated is the schedule he asked about.

quests.question:
The library extended its hours during exams, but students said this didn't help those who lived off campus.
What does 'this' refer to?
quests.sentence: The library extended its hours during exams, but students said this didn't help those who lived off campus.
quests.hint: What did students say didn't help?
quests.explanation: Remember that 'this' sums up what the library did in the first clause. It is the extension of hours that did not help.

quests.question:
Customer: My blender stopped working after two weeks. I emailed the shop, but they haven't answered. Agent: I'm sorry. I'll ask them to send a replacement.
Who is 'they' pointing back to?
quests.sentence: Customer: My blender stopped working after two weeks. I emailed the shop, but they haven't answered. Agent: I'm sorry. I'll ask them to send a replacement.
quests.hint: Who was emailed?
quests.explanation: In this sentence, 'they' is the people or business that received the email and did not reply. The customer wrote the message.

quests.question:
The agent told Mr. Reddy the parcel had left the depot, but he said he'd heard that once already and asked her to escalate the complaint.
In this text, who does 'her' stand for?
quests.sentence: The agent told Mr. Reddy the parcel had left the depot, but he said he'd heard that once already and asked her to escalate the complaint.
quests.hint: Who can escalate a complaint?
quests.explanation: Note that 'her' is feminine, and Mr. Reddy is male. The agent is the person who can escalate his complaint.

quests.question:
If the seals are broken when your parcel arrives, please do not open it and contact us within forty-eight hours.
What is being referred to by 'it'?
quests.sentence: If the seals are broken when your parcel arrives, please do not open it and contact us within forty-eight hours.
quests.hint: What should not be opened?
quests.explanation: 'It' is the object of 'open'. The seals are broken, but what you do not open is the parcel.

quests.question:
Priya booked a room at the guesthouse for her parents. When they arrived, the owner said theirs hadn't been prepared yet.
What is being referred to by 'theirs'?
quests.sentence: Priya booked a room at the guesthouse for her parents. When they arrived, the owner said theirs hadn't been prepared yet.
quests.hint: 'Theirs' means 'their ___'. Who arrived?
quests.explanation: Remember that 'theirs' is plural and refers to those who just arrived, her parents. It stands for the room booked for them.

quests.question:
The conductor asked the couple to show their tickets, but he couldn't scan them because the barcodes were smudged.
What is meant by 'them'?
quests.sentence: The conductor asked the couple to show their tickets, but he couldn't scan them because the barcodes were smudged.
quests.hint: What did he try to scan?
quests.explanation: Here, 'them' is the object of 'scan'. What was to be scanned is the tickets, since people and the conductor cannot be scanned.

quests.question:
Our train was cancelled, so we asked the station manager for a refund. She said she couldn't authorise it herself and passed us to the regional office.
Who is meant by 'herself'?
quests.sentence: Our train was cancelled, so we asked the station manager for a refund. She said she couldn't authorise it herself and passed us to the regional office.
quests.hint: Who could not authorise the refund?
quests.explanation: Here, 'herself' is feminine singular and stresses who could not decide alone. That is the station manager who was asked.

quests.question:
The nurse told Mr. Ferrari that the doctor would see him after the blood test and that he shouldn't eat until it was done.
What is being referred to by 'it'?
quests.sentence: The nurse told Mr. Ferrari that the doctor would see him after the blood test and that he shouldn't eat until it was done.
quests.hint: What must be finished before he eats?
quests.explanation: 'It' is what must be done before he eats. A fast before a blood test ends when the test is over.

quests.question:
Your test results are back. Your GP will call you if she needs to change your medication; otherwise, continue taking it as before.
What does 'it' point back to?
quests.sentence: Your test results are back. Your GP will call you if she needs to change your medication; otherwise, continue taking it as before.
quests.hint: What are you taking?
quests.explanation: In this sentence, 'it' is singular and is what you continue taking. Medication is taken; a GP and results are not.

quests.question:
The pharmacist explained that the tablets should be taken with food and that patients who forget a dose shouldn't take two together, because that could cause side effects.
What does 'that' point back to?
quests.sentence: The pharmacist explained that the tablets should be taken with food and that patients who forget a dose shouldn't take two together, because that could cause side effects.
quests.hint: What could cause side effects?
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the reason for the warning. The warning is about taking two together, so 'that' refers to that action.

quests.question:
The update installed overnight, but the app it was meant to fix still crashes.
What is being referred to by 'it'?
quests.sentence: The update installed overnight, but the app it was meant to fix still crashes.
quests.hint: What was meant to fix something?
quests.explanation: Note that 'it' is the subject of 'was meant to fix'. The update is what was meant to fix the app, and the app is the thing being fixed.

quests.question:
Log in with your email address and password. If you have forgotten it, choose 'Reset' and we will send a link to the address you registered.
What does 'it' refer to?
quests.sentence: Log in with your email address and password. If you have forgotten it, choose 'Reset' and we will send a link to the address you registered.
quests.hint: What might you forget and need to reset?
quests.explanation: Look closely: 'it' is singular and is what you would reset. You have not forgotten the address, because the link is sent to it.

quests.question:
The developers shipped the patch before the testers had finished their checks, which is why it introduced new bugs.
What is 'it' pointing back to?
quests.sentence: The developers shipped the patch before the testers had finished their checks, which is why it introduced new bugs.
quests.hint: What introduced the bugs?
quests.explanation: The pronoun 'it' is the thing that was shipped too early. The patch is what introduced the bugs, while the checks were unfinished.

quests.question:
We have sent you a replacement card. Please destroy the old one and activate the new one as soon as it arrives.
What does 'it' refer to?
quests.sentence: We have sent you a replacement card. Please destroy the old one and activate the new one as soon as it arrives.
quests.hint: What is arriving?
quests.explanation: 'It' arrives, and the sentence has just told you the replacement is on its way. The old card is already with you.

quests.question:
The adviser told the couple they could send money abroad without a fee if they used the app, though she recommended they compare it with other services.
In this text, what does 'it' stand for?
quests.sentence: The adviser told the couple they could send money abroad without a fee if they used the app, though she recommended they compare it with other services.
quests.hint: What would be compared with other services?
quests.explanation: 'Compare it with other services' needs a service. The app is the service being recommended and needing comparison.

quests.question:
Mr. Wong asked the bank to freeze his account after his wallet was stolen. It agreed at once, but it warned him that standing orders would still go out.
What does 'it' (the first one) refer to?
quests.sentence: Mr. Wong asked the bank to freeze his account after his wallet was stolen. It agreed at once, but it warned him that standing orders would still go out.
quests.hint: Who agreed and gave a warning?
quests.explanation: Note that 'it' is the one who agreed and warned. Only the bank can act and speak; the account and wallet are objects.

quests.question:
I ordered a jacket and a pair of boots online. It arrived on Monday, but they are still on the way.
What is meant by 'they'?
quests.sentence: I ordered a jacket and a pair of boots online. It arrived on Monday, but they are still on the way.
quests.hint: 'They' is plural. Which item is plural?
quests.explanation: Remember that 'they' is plural. The jacket is single and has already arrived, while the boots are the plural item still coming.

quests.question:
The label says the sweater must be washed by hand, but Elif put it in the machine, and it shrank.
What does 'it' (the last one) refer to?
quests.sentence: The label says the sweater must be washed by hand, but Elif put it in the machine, and it shrank.
quests.hint: What could shrink?
quests.explanation: 'It' is what shrank. A sweater can shrink in a wash, while the machine and the label cannot.

quests.question:
The store will refund any item that is returned within thirty days, provided it is unworn and has its tags attached.
What is meant by 'its'?
quests.sentence: The store will refund any item that is returned within thirty days, provided it is unworn and has its tags attached.
quests.hint: What has tags attached?
quests.explanation: 'Its tags' belong to the item, and the condition 'unworn' also describes it. The store does not need tags on itself.

quests.question:
Residents must put their bins out by seven on collection day. The council will not take bags that are left beside them.
What is being referred to by 'them'?
quests.sentence: Residents must put their bins out by seven on collection day. The council will not take bags that are left beside them.
quests.hint: Where are bags left?
quests.explanation: 'Beside them' names the place where bags are left. The bags are beside the bins, not beside the people.

quests.question:
Applicants who submit the form online should keep the reference number, which they will need if they wish to check its status.
In this text, what does 'its' stand for?
quests.sentence: Applicants who submit the form online should keep the reference number, which they will need if they wish to check its status.
quests.hint: What has a status that you check with a number?
quests.explanation: 'Its status' is the status of the submitted form. The reference number is the key used to look it up.

quests.question:
Visitors are asked to hand in any object they find, and staff will contact whoever owns it.
What is meant by 'it'?
quests.sentence: Visitors are asked to hand in any object they find, and staff will contact whoever owns it.
quests.hint: What could be owned?
quests.explanation: 'It' is the thing owned by someone. Only the object handed in has an owner.

quests.question:
Dr. Malik's assistant called Mr. Nwosu to say that his appointment had been moved because the doctor was needed at the hospital.
Whose appointment does 'his' refer to?
quests.sentence: Dr. Malik's assistant called Mr. Nwosu to say that his appointment had been moved because the doctor was needed at the hospital.
quests.hint: Who has an appointment that can be moved?
quests.explanation: The person called about the change is the patient. The appointment is Mr. Nwosu's, and the doctor is the one being needed elsewhere.

quests.question:
'Have you told Mum about the party?' 'Not yet. I'll ask Dad first, because he'll want to invite his colleagues, and then it will be too big for the flat.'
What is 'it' pointing back to?
quests.sentence: 'Have you told Mum about the party?' 'Not yet. I'll ask Dad first, because he'll want to invite his colleagues, and then it will be too big for the flat.'
quests.hint: What could become too big once extra guests are invited?
quests.explanation: Notice that 'it' is singular and non-human, so it cannot be Mum or Dad. Inviting extra colleagues would make the party too big for the flat.

quests.question:
Please bring your child's vaccination record and your own ID to the clinic. Staff will scan yours at the desk and return it before you leave.
What is 'yours' pointing back to?
quests.sentence: Please bring your child's vaccination record and your own ID to the clinic. Staff will scan yours at the desk and return it before you leave.
quests.hint: 'Yours' means 'your ___'. Which item is contrasted with the child's?
quests.explanation: 'Yours' is set against 'your child's' record, so it refers to the parent's own item: the ID. The record belongs to the child.
